newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER.

text.p: Morocco's bourse closed 0.08 percent higher on Wednesday, lifted mainly by the largest capitalisation firms such as ONA, SNI and BCM, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 666.13 points from 665.62 points on Tuesday, a bourse official said.

"Generally speaking, bourse activity was normal...Nearly 80,000 shares changed hands today, of which 50 percent was on the over the counter market where Moroccan banks and insurance firms are active," a stockbroker said.
Total traded volume was down to 98.9 million dirhams from 129.3 million in the previous session, the broker said.
A volume of 46.3 million dirhams was exchanged on the official market, he added.
With a market capitalisation of 14.2 billion dirhams, ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, gained two dirhams to close at 832 dirhams.
Its three listed subsidiaries Cosumar, Centrale Laitiere and Financiere Diwan rose between six and eight dirhams. They closed respectively at 860, 2,758 and 362 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's second largest capitalisation firm, rose five dirhams to 915 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private group with diversified stakes in more than 40 companies, was up six dirhams to close at 792 dirhams.
The country's largest oil refiner Societe Marocaine de l'Industrie du Raffinage (Samir) remained stable at 337 dirhams.
Consumer credit firm Maghrebail, the session's best performer, jumped 32 dirhams to close at 565 dirhams.
